newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Agrobanka Slovak unit seeks independence.
newsitem.headline: Agrobanka Slovak unit seeks independence.

text.p: The Slovak unit of the Czech-based bank Agrobanka a.s., said on Wednesday that the bank's Slovak operation was seeking to become a fully-independent bank by the beginning of 1997.

Vranislav Petroch, director of Agrobanka's Slovak unit, told a news conference that the plan would be for Agrobanka sro Czech Republic to hold 34 percent of the new bank's basic equity of one billion crowns with five large Slovak companies holding the remainder.

"(Agrobanka Slovakia) wants to create an independent bank with one billion crowns basic capital in which it would have 34 percent and the remaining 66 percent would be held by domestic investors," Petroch said at the news conference held during a banking trade show in central Slovakia.
He said that an application was made in August to the National Bank of Slovakia for a full banking licence.
Petroch said the five companies, which he declined to specifically name, would be lucrative Slovak companies from the chemical industry of which only one has some commitments to Agrobanka."

The announcement comes one day after the Czech parent was put under temporary forced administration by the Czech National Bank because of poor liquidity stemming from the failure of another Czech bank, Kreditni Banka a.s.
Petroch said the Slovak operations of Agrobanka were "fully liquid and fully capable of fulfilling any requests by clients".
He said the guarantees for Agrobanka creditors made the Czech National Bank on Tuesday would still apply to the new Slovak bank if approved.
Petroch said that Agrobanka Slovakia had three billion Slovak crowns in deposits and about 150 million had been withdrawn since the Czech announcement on Tuesday.

The Slovak central bank's governing board is scheduled to hold an extraordinary meeting in Banska Bystrica later on Wednesday, but it is not yet clear whether the Agrobanka application will be discussed.
